thread:
alice_support: Hi — Janeway from Acme hit us with intermittent 401s when calling their Dedicated model endpoint through their VPC LB. They say Authorization: Bearer is present client-side and works for a while, then starts failing (~5–15m). Can someone triage?
customer_janeway: repro steps: curl to my-vpc.example.com -> LB -> dedicated gw. Sample: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...' https://my-vpc.example.com/v1/generate
> HTTP/2 401
< {"error":"unauthorized","reason":"invalid_token"}
```
We log the header on our side and it looks correct when request arrives, but our auth service rejects token intermittently.
alice_support: attaching the raw proxy logs and gw traces now.
deploy-bot: [deploy] dedicated-gateway v2.14 rolled at 2026-03-10T02:11Z (tag: release-2.14.1)
bob_infra: quick question — is the LB doing any header rewriting or cookie-to-header conversion? Some vendors splice auth into a cookie and rewrite to Authorization.
customer_janeway: yes, their managed LB (vendor F5) is doing a signed-cookie -> Authorization rewrite for legacy clients. We only recently enabled keepalive pooling.
carla_platform: can you paste the gateway incoming raw headers for a failing request and a succeeding one (byte-for-byte)? We need to compare Authorization header content.
customer_janeway: failing request (redacted):
```
:authority: my-vpc.example.com
:method: POST
authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIU...AA==
content-type: application/json
cookie: auth_cookie=eyJhbGciOiJIU...AA==; other=1
```
Succeeding request shows same token string in cookie + Authorization.
dave_runtime: looking at our ext-authz trace for the failing call: 
```
ext_authz: received token header length=256
ext_authz: parsed jwt claims: sub=svc-123 aud=redwood-inference exp=... nonce="abc123"
ext_authz: signature verification FAILED (nonce claim mismatch)
```
nonce claim mismatch is odd — nonce is included in token payload. If the value got mutated that would break signature.
elaine_security: F5 rewrite path often URL-encodes or trims some characters when moving cookie -> header. If they base64-url encode differently or strip padding '=' at the end, signature breaks. Also check for newline/whitespace injection.
bob_infra: I asked customer to capture tcpdump between LB and gw. They sent a pcap snippet. I inspected the Authorization header bytes: trailing '=' characters are missing in some requests (padding removed) — cookie carried full base64, rewrite removed padding.
carla_platform: that fits. Some JWT libs accept unpadded base64, but our token issuer included padding as part of signature input. When padding removed, signature fails. Why only intermittent? likely due to different code path in LB: cookie path uses function A that preserves padding, header rewrite uses function B that strips '=' when cookie length > 200. Could be triggered by keepalive or chunking.
alice_support: customer reported failures started after enabling keepalive pooling on LB last week.
dave_runtime: short-term mitigation: gateway can detect Authorization header and, if length mod 4 != 0, attempt to restore padding before verification (i.e., add '=' chars) for incoming tokens that look base64-like. I'll prototype a permissive decoder that tries padded and unpadded forms.
elaine_security: caution — permissive fixes expand attack surface. Limit to internal VPC networks or trusted LB IP ranges, and add strict logging. Also recommend vendor config change as primary fix.
carla_platform: customer workaround: configure F5 rewrite to not modify cookie payload or to write to X-Forwarded-Authorization header instead of Authorization (some rewrites canonicalize values less). Another safe option: configure LB to preserve exact bytes.
bob_infra: asked Acme to open a ticket with vendor and temporary rule: preserve cookie base64 padding. They confirmed vendor change queued (ETA 48h).
alice_support: for tracking, I'm adding a ticket: SR-2026-1487. Action items: 
- bob_infra: confirm vendor fix applied and share patch
- dave_runtime: push permissive decoder behind feature flag gated by allowlist IPs
- elaine_security: write caveat for risk and approve allowlist

dave_runtime: prototype ready, will roll to canary tomorrow in dedicated-gateway with env var JWT_PAD_TOLERANT=true for customer IPs.
customer_janeway: confirmed canary test with patched gw fixed the failing requests in our smoke tests. Thanks.
elaine_security: record shows root cause = LB cookie->header rewrite stripping base64 padding on some rewrite path. We'll close once vendor rollout and we remove allowlist.
alice_support: closing loop with customer and scheduling follow-up. Marking as resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
